name: Kinetic-Anchored Screened Khronon
claimed_mechanism: An auxiliary Legendre scalar chi implements the frozen mu(y) MOND relation in the deep-MOND limit while the matter sector is minimally coupled to the single physical metric. A khronon T supplies a preferred-frame direction, and its matter-current coupling is multiplied by e^{-y}, so the preferred-frame response is screened in the large-y branch. A separate multiplier lambda is fixed by an independent constraint to a finite constant, and it multiplies the tensor kinetic term, so the propagating-mode normalization is not generated by the screened khronon coupling.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit the metric reduces to Newtonian gravity plus the chi-generated MOND correction, with the usual a0 scaling in the deep-MOND regime. The khronon-induced preferred-frame anisotropy is proportional to e^{-y}, so it is suppressed when y is large and remains finite when y is small. The tensor mode has a finite kinetic coefficient set by lambda, giving a well-defined propagation speed and no collision between screening and kinetic normalization.
inequivalence_argument: This is not a coefficient tweak of a killed architecture because it changes the canonical field content and constraint hierarchy by adding an independent kinetic-anchor multiplier and an auxiliary Legendre chi sector. The screened preferred-frame coupling and the propagating tensor kinetic term are controlled by different fields, so the P7 collision is structurally absent rather than avoided by rescaling G or altering mu(y). It is inequivalent to dead classes that either identify the tensor kinetic normalization with the screened coupling, remove the preferred-frame sector, or rely on nonlocal or multi-sector screening, because here the screening factor acts only on the khronon-current interaction while lambda fixes the tensor kinetic independently.
